name: Munich
industries: Automotive, industrial engineering, insurance and a deep technology sector give Munich Germany's richest project market.
intro:
Munich pairs Germany's most valuable corporations with its highest salaries, and its project culture reflects the neighbourhood: BMW's vehicle programmes, Siemens's global engineering portfolios, Allianz's transformation agenda and a dense ring of technology suppliers. These organisations run delivery at international scale, which is precisely where PMP earns its keep — while Munich's software and automotive-software teams, including major US tech offices, hire on Scrum credentials. Certification pays for itself faster here than almost anywhere in Europe. We run live online cohorts throughout the year on Munich-friendly hours — weekend Saturday–Sunday batches and midweek Wednesday–Thursday batches both — meaning learners in Munich attend at ordinary local times, never overnight; the table below shows each upcoming date converted for Munich. We then guide your exam application, provide full-length mocks, and stay available for doubts until the certificate arrives.

Munich is corporate Germany's engineering capital — automotive, industrial technology, insurance and the DAX ecosystem around them — and its projects run with the process rigor those industries are famous for. Certified project professionals fit those governance structures on day one, which is why Munich job postings name credentials more often than anywhere else in the country. The course runs live online across two days in central European hours, delivered in English as most international programs here are. Munich salaries lead Germany for certified project roles; the sourced entries below give current, dated figures rather than survey folklore. The employer list shows the automotive-industrial-insurance base hiring certified talent, and engineering organizations can certify project departments together through private cohorts.
